# WO-2026-08-12-B15-VISION-03 — Round 3: omission root cause, AC5 residual, general dedup

## Acceptance criteria

AC1 (= acceptance_property, the omission investigation — the largest failure class, previously
untargeted): **Investigate first, using Asdair's actual raw run data
(`C:\Users\Buggly\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Fusion247PKA\65635422-06ce-4e12-8614-a5e21fb76876\scratchpad\asdair-vision-test\round2\run-a.json`
and `run-b.json`, plus his ground-truth list in `score.mjs` in the same folder) before writing any fix.**
Determine which of these (or another cause) actually explains the omissions: (a) generated regions don't
fully cover the photo — some lines fall in gaps or off an edge; (b) the model sees a region but reports
nothing for some lines within it (a generation/attention limit on a dense region); (c) a line IS read by
the model but is filtered out somewhere in the pipeline before reaching the final output (a bug, not a
model limit); (d) something else. **A plausible, unverified hypothesis, not a prescribed answer**: the
current design flags SUSPECT lines for re-inspection, but has no mechanism to flag a region that
produced ZERO lines as itself suspicious — silence isn't currently treated as an anomaly. Verify or
falsify this against the real data before building around it. Fix whatever the actual cause turns out to
be; report the true cause either way, even if it isn't the hypothesis above.

AC2: **The AC5 residual — why did TRESemme/Lucozade Raspberry reappear despite a DB-level fix testing
clean?** Round 2's `lineProvenance.js` fix was proven against synthetic test fixtures with no live
gateway call; Asdair's diagnostic never touches the database at all. So the live reappearance is
evidence about the VISION/INTERPRETATION layer, not proof the DB fix is wrong. Investigate whether the
model is independently re-hallucinating these specific items on the photo (a prompt/grounding issue,
not a DB issue), and if so, fix it there — do not assume the round-2 DB fix needs undoing without
evidence it's actually implicated.

AC3: Generalise the duplicate-collapsing mechanism beyond the single Vanish case round 2 fixed — the
live re-test found a NEW instance of the same defect shape (two different Febreze products collapsed
into one confident line). Fix the general case, proven by a test that would have caught the Febreze
shape specifically, not just re-confirming the already-fixed Vanish case.

AC4: Yazoo Chocolate — now confirmed unstable in two different shapes across two live runs (wrong
quantity in one, omitted in the other). If AC1's omission-root-cause fix explains the omission case,
confirm it also explains Yazoo specifically; if the wrong-quantity case is a separate cause, name and
fix it, or report precisely why it resists a confident fix — round 1 and round 2 both correctly declined
to guess-fix this; round 3 should either close it or explain exactly why it's still open.

AC5: All touched-package tests pass with a non-zero executed count, including DB-gated tests via the
disposable-Postgres pattern already established.

AC6: Update (do not execute) the diagnostic harness so a future live re-test can distinguish "line never
generated by any region" from "line generated then filtered/dropped" from "line genuinely never seen by
the model" — whichever AC1 finds the real cause to be, make it observable in the harness output for the
next live re-test, not just fixed silently.

## Required evidence

- The AC1 root-cause finding itself, stated plainly, with the specific evidence from Asdair's raw run
  JSONs that supports it (quote the actual data, don't assert a conclusion without it).
- The exact test output for AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4 — paste real assertions and results.
